Resolution: There are two possible solutions for this issue.
1. Deploy the System Monitoring for WebSphere Application Server again. Once the shared service is deployed, attempt the uninstall again.
2. Manually remove the WebSphere Application Server configuration that is specific to ITCAM and is causing this issue. For information about manual removal, refer to the ITCAM topic the Related Information below.

ibm.itcamfapps_ad.doc_72/was_agent_install_guide_dist/was_agent_
   shared/chapter_ads_dc/rmap_customizingrequestinformationmapping.
   html
   *
   ****************************************************************
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The fix for this APAR is contained in the following maintenance
   release:
   
    | interim fix | 7.2.0.0.-TIV-ITCAM_DC-IF0015

*  The SDA support description and the need to manually install
   TEPS support is documented here:
   http://www-03preprod.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SS3JRN_7.2. [http://www-03preprod.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SS3JRN_7.2.]
   1/com.ibm.itcamfapps_soa.doc_7201/soa_install_guide/sda_support.
   html?cp=SS3JRN_7.2.1.1%2F15-2-2-1-2-0
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

COMMENTS

DC_home/itcamdc/etc/was/dcInput_manual.properties 

into 

DC_home/runtime/profile_name.cell_name.node_name.server_name.DCManualInput.txt. 

Then, when you edit the contents of the file to configure the DC communication with a MS installed on Windows, you need paying attention to two things:

1- Make sure that variable FILESEP is set like this:

FILESEP=/

There should be only one slash for a Windows MS


2. Set the variable ms.home in the following format:

ms.home=F:\\ibm\\itcam\\WebSphere\\MS

ms.home should have a Windows path with two slashes.

In case of a path containing blank spaces, you can use double quotes like this:

ms.home="C:\\Program Files\\IBM\\itcam\\WebSphere\\MS"
